# Panelary

> Leak-safe, Polars-native feature engineering and ML for panel data (many entities observed over time). Panelary is a panel-first (entity x time) data-science toolkit with an sklearn-familiar API, lazy Polars execution, and correctness-by-construction: no lookahead, ever. Version 0.4.0 is pure Python (the Rust extension was dropped) and ships a single universal `py3-none-any` wheel with `py.typed`. Built on the foundations of functime (Apache-2.0) and licensed Apache-2.0.

Pipeline philosophy: transform -> interact -> map -> extract -> select -> synthesize -> compare -> label -> signal_eval -> models -> model_selection, with no lookahead at any stage.

## Naming and install

- Project/brand name: Panelary. Python import and PyPI package: `panelary`. The public rename to `panelary` is planned but NOT effective — `import panelary` does not work. Use `import panelary as pk`.
- Requires Python >= 3.10. Mandatory dependencies are only `numpy` and `polars>=1.0.0`; everything heavier is an optional extra.
- Install: `pip install panelary`, or `pip install "panelary[recommended]"` for the batteries-included set, or `[all]` for everything. 22 extras exist, including `ml`, `scipy`, `lightgbm`, `catboost`, `xgboost`, `forecasting`, `automl`, `seasonality`, `dimreduce`, `explain`, `llm`, `cafe`, `viz`, `signatures`, `fast`, `progress`, `ann`, `gpu`, `docs`, `dev`.
- A missing optional dependency raises an actionable error naming the extra to install (via `panelary._deps.require`), never a bare ImportError.

## Core concepts

- PanelFrame: a typed, lazy view over a long-format panel keyed by `(entity, time)`. Construct with `pk.PanelFrame(df, entity="ticker", time="date")`; read back via `.entity_col` / `.time_col`. The unit of work is the panel, not a bag of rows.
- panel_safe contract: within-entity operations stay inside their entity and run in time order (`.over(entity_col)` on a time-sorted panel).
- leakage_safe contract: cross-sectional operations are per-date (`.over(time_col)`), and anything with a `fit` step is fit per fold on training data only — never globally, never on the test fold.
- Prefix invariance: `f(x[:T])[t] == f(x[:T+k])[t]` for `t <= T`. No window size, threshold, lag order or normalisation constant may depend on total series length.
- Leak-safe Pipeline: sklearn-style `fit`/`transform` pipeline where scalers and selectors are fit per fold.
- Purged cross-validation: `PurgedKFold` and `CombinatorialPurgedCV` (CPCV) apply purging and embargo to remove train/test leakage around fold boundaries.
- Expression namespaces: operators are called as `pl.col(...).<namespace>.<name>(...)` across the `panel`, `xs`, `ts` and `factor` namespaces. `.panel` implies `.over(entity)`; `.xs` implies `.over(time)`. Typed `.pyi` stubs ship in the wheel.
- Operator registry: `pk.registry` holds a `FeatureSpec` per operator recording signature, input/output shape, tier, `panel_safe`/`leakage_safe` flags, and provenance/license. `registry.to_records()` serialises it, `registry.to_llms_txt()` renders a machine-readable operator catalogue, and `registry.audit()` checks that every operator is permissively licensed. 56 operators are registered today (`ts`=42, `xs`=7, `factor`=4, `panel`=3).

## Shipped modules (0.4.0)

- `pk.core` — the correctness kernel: `PanelFrame`, leak-safe `Pipeline`, `PanelTransformer`/`PanelEstimator` protocols, purged model selection.
- `pk.transform` — panel-native, leak-safe preprocessing: winsorize/scaling, `frac_diff`, ranking, neutralization.
- `pk.label` — leak-safe labeling (Lopez de Prado, AFML Ch. 3): `triple_barrier` and friends.
- `pk.select` — leak-safe feature selection (supervised and unsupervised), fit per fold.
- `pk.factor` — cross-sectional factor evaluation: information coefficients, neutralization, portfolio construction.
- `pk.reduce` — leak-safe dimensionality reduction: PCA, ICA, hierarchical factor analysis, robust factors, factor-count selection.
- `pk.cluster` — leak-safe panel clustering, including cross-sectional and k-Shape.
- `pk.econ` — panel and time-series econometrics: HDFE, Fama-MacBeth, IVX, DML, connectedness, plus an econometric feature suite (EVT, HAR-RV, liquidity, long memory, Nelson-Siegel, unit roots).
- `pk.explain` — leak-safe, panel-aware feature attribution (SHAP): tree and estimator backends, interactions, stability, aggregation.
- `pk.validation` — honest validation and selection: bootstraps, CV, forecast tests, selection statistics.
- `panelary.detect` — causal detection of explosive regimes, bubbles and change points (GSADF/BSADF, CUSUM/FOCuS monitors, panel breadth). NOTE: shipped as a subpackage but not yet re-exported on the top-level `pk` namespace; import it as `import panelary.detect as detect`.
- `pk.forecasting` / `pk.models` — forecaster and panel/cross-sectional model wrappers (linear, kNN, LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, AutoML, conformal, censored).
- `pk.metrics`, `pk.evaluation`, `pk.backtesting` — point, probabilistic and multi-objective metrics; deflated Sharpe ratio; probability of backtest overfitting.
- `pk.seasonality` — calendar and Fourier seasonal features.
- `pk.catch22`, `pk.feature_extractors`, `pk.extract_features` — time-series feature extraction, including a clean-room catch22 reimplementation.
- `pk.imputation` / `pk.CafeImputer` — leak-safe imputation.
- `pk.llm` — optional LLM-assisted analysis of panels.
- `pk.assert_no_lookahead`, `pk.testing` — the leakage verifier and test helpers.

## Ecosystem positioning

- Complements polars-ds and polars_ta (general Polars-native primitives); does not compete with them.
- Nixtla (statsforecast/mlforecast) owns general forecasting; Panelary centers on leak-safe feature engineering, labeling, selection, attribution and cross-sectional ML for panels.
- catch22 features are clean-room reimplemented from Lubba et al. (2019), NOT vendored from the GPL `pycatch22`.
